From Coal Miners to Naval Warriors: A Tribute Crafted from Scrap!

As a tribute to the Indian Navy’s unwavering commitment to safeguarding the nation’s maritime frontiers, Eastern Coalfields Limited (ECL) presented a specially crafted model of a warship to the 1 Bengal NCC Naval Unit. Made from discarded components of coal mining machinery, the model symbolises the shared spirit of dedication, service and nation-building that unites coal miners and naval personnel.

The model was meticulously crafted at ECL’s Neamatpur Central Workshop under the ‘Waste to Wealth’ initiative of Special Campaign 6. The creation showcases the ingenuity and craftsmanship of ECL’s workforce while promoting resource reutilisation and sustainability.

On behalf of Dr. Satish Jha, Chairman-cum-Managing Director, ECL, the Functional Directors and the entire ECL Parivar, Maj. S. Tiwari, Chief of Security, ECL, accompanied by Ms. Nishchal Soni, Manager (HR), Neamatpur Central Workshop, presented the model to Commodore Caesar Basu and Commander Sanjib Saran of the Indian Navy as a gesture of gratitude and respect.

From the depths of coal mines to the vast expanse of the seas, the spirit of serving the nation unites us all.

Market Closing Wrap | October 30, 2026

Nifty closed green, but the broader market tells a completely different story!

Nifty reclaimed 23,000, supported largely by IT and pharma heavyweights. Beneath the surface, selling pressure remained intense across midcaps and smallcaps.

Market Scorecard
• Nifty 50: 23,053 (+0.51%)
• Sensex: 74,460 (+0.42%)
• Bank Nifty: 54,687 (-0.41%)
• Midcaps: -0.90%
• Smallcaps: -1.85%

Market Breadth
• Advances: 1,311
• Declines: 2,862

More than twice as many stocks declined as advanced. That tells you how narrow this recovery really is!

Sector Rotation
• IT (+2.3%) and Pharma (+1.6%) led the recovery.
• Infosys, Coforge and Persistent continued attracting interest.
• Defence (-2.3%), Capital Markets, Media and Consumer Durables remained under pressure.
• PSU Banks, Auto and broader smallcaps also witnessed selling.

Money appears to be rotating out of high-beta sectors into a handful of large-cap names.

Stocks in Focus
• Trent: +5.4% following strong earnings.
• IndiGo: +3.4% as improving operating performance supported sentiment.
• Infosys: +2.7%, benefiting from IT sector strength.
• Laurus Labs: Fresh record highs following strong earnings momentum.
• Equitas SFB: Sharp two-day correction despite record profitability, with the CEO's exit weighing on sentiment.

Macro Picture
• USD/INR hovering around 95.25.
• RBI repo rate at 5.50%.
• Q2 GDP growth estimated around 7.35%.
• Brent crude near $113–115.

Elevated crude prices, currency pressure and rising global yields remain important risks for Indian equities.

Institutional Flows (Thursday)
• FII: Net sellers of 944 Cr
• DII: Net buyers of 1,924 Cr

Domestic institutions continue absorbing part of the foreign selling pressure.

Nifty Levels for Monday, November 2

Support: 22,905 / 22,800
Resistance: 23,118–23,160 / 23,250

A sustained move above 23,160 could improve short-term momentum. Losing 22,905 may invite renewed selling pressure.

Stocks on My Radar
• Reliance: Q2 results could influence Monday's index direction.
• Trent: Watch 3,049.90 for upside confirmation.
• IndiGo: 4,869 remains an important breakout level.
• Laurus Labs: Strong momentum, but stretched valuations and sharp volatility warrant caution.

My Take:

An index gaining 0.5% while nearly 70% of stocks decline is hardly a broad-based recovery.

This looks more like selective institutional rotation than a genuine market-wide reversal.

Until market breadth improves and midcaps and smallcaps start participating, I would treat every index recovery with caution.

The index may be green, but most portfolios are probably telling a different story!

The Mahanadi Coalfields IPO is an OFS. Every rupee of that ₹10,000 crore goes to Coal India, not to the coal miner itself.

That distinction matters. A fresh issue puts money into the company for capex or debt paydown. An OFS means existing holders cashing out. Here, the seller is the parent PSU, and the company gets zero from its own listing.

Mahanadi produced 218 million tonnes in FY26, about 21% of India’s coal output. Solid numbers. But you are buying shares from Coal India, not funding Mahanadi’s growth.

I find this interesting because it means the valuation depends entirely on what the market thinks Mahanadi is worth as a standalone entity, not on any new investment story. The parent gets the liquidity, and you get a separately traded PSU.

If the company needed capital, I would look closer. Here, the question is whether the price leaves room after the parent unlocks value. That is the only number that decides it for me. ⛏️

#Coforge: The shift from selling manpower to delivering AI-powered business outcomes.

Interesting developments from the Q2FY27 conference call.

1/ AI is moving from experimentation to actual business operations.

Coforge is already working on 520+ AI engagements across 225+ clients, with 260+ AI agents deployed in live operations.

The focus is shifting from building chatbots to automating actual business processes.

2/ Building an enterprise AI ecosystem.

Coforge has introduced four important AI initiatives:

• Nuuron – Connects enterprise data, knowledge, processes and decision-making to provide business context to AI agents.

• Forge-X, https://t.co/dXOGuFkGYJ and https://t.co/tjLSVrjCaP – AI solutions for software engineering, IT operations and business processes.

• Momentuum Blue – Specialised engineers who work directly with clients to take AI solutions from pilot projects to large-scale deployment.

• AI Launchpad – Helps enterprises select and deploy different AI models while maintaining control over costs, data and intellectual property.

3/ AI is becoming an internal margin-expansion tool.

Perhaps the most important development.

Coforge is embedding AI into its existing fixed-price contracts.

Earlier, a project might require 100 engineers. AI can potentially help complete the same work with fewer people, reducing delivery costs while retaining the contracted revenue.

Management expects these productivity benefits to become increasingly visible in margins from Q4FY27.

4/ A major opportunity in legacy modernisation.

Many banks, insurance companies and large enterprises still depend on decades-old software systems.

Coforge is using AI to understand, modernise and migrate these complicated systems.

One of its largest programmes involves migrating 12 million lines of code from a machine-language platform to Google Cloud over approximately 4.5 years.

This is much more than ordinary software development. It requires deep technical expertise and an understanding of the client's business.

5/ Moving towards value-based selling instead of price-based competition.

Coforge is increasingly developing solutions proactively rather than simply participating in competitive vendor bidding.

Management highlighted that most of its large deals are proactively developed and often sole-sourced.

The objective is to solve specific business problems instead of competing purely on the number of developers and project costs.

This could help protect margins in an industry facing pricing pressure.

6/ Encora is adding strategic capabilities beyond revenue.

The acquisition is strengthening Coforge's presence across Eastern Europe and Latin America.

More importantly, both companies can now cross-sell capabilities across their customer bases.

The largest deal currently being pursued by Coforge is from an Encora client.

This creates an additional growth opportunity beyond cost synergies.

7/ An interesting shift in enterprise AI demand.

Coforge's opportunity is expanding beyond software coding into areas such as:

• Insurance underwriting and claims processes.
• Banking KYC and compliance workflows.
• Enterprise data integration.
• Legacy system modernisation.
• AI-powered customer service.
• Automated business operations.

These are complex enterprise problems where domain knowledge and integration capabilities matter.

My takeaway:

The biggest structural opportunity at Coforge is not simply selling AI software.

It is helping enterprises make AI work inside their existing business processes, data systems and legacy infrastructure.

At the same time, Coforge is using AI internally to deliver projects more efficiently.

Selling AI to clients while using AI to improve its own profitability could become a powerful combination.

The key thing to track from here: Can AI-led productivity translate into sustained gross-margin and EBIT-margin expansion without compromising growth?

What happens when 'Earnings' eventually outrun the 'Index'? 

​we all know that stock prices and business profits mostly never move together in shorter timeframes. Short term price action is nothing but just noise which is always part of the whole saga . Give it 5 or 10 years though & guess what : "profits or bottom line finally take over" ! 💯 
But, e​very now & then a wide gap opens up. Profits grow for years while the index stays flat. The market gets cheaper without needing a price crash because the PE ratio gets squeezed down.
​Since 2000 a gap wider than 6% between 5 yr rolling EPS growth and 5 yr index returns appeared only four times in India: 2004, 2008, 2022 and right now in October 2026.
​Right now 5 yr rolling Nifty 500 returns are around 7.7% annualized while corporate EPS grew 14.1%. This lag has actually pulled broad market PE down from 27x to under 21x.

​When profits grow 14% but prices move 7.7%, the market is just digesting old overvaluation. Companies use profits to pay down debt instead of chasing empty revenue growth. The business gets safer even if headline stock prices look dull.
​On top of that, global macro worries and FII selling keep index levels down while domestic businesses keep making money. Nowadays we see that majority of retail investors trade momentum anyway. When an index stays flat for two years people get bored and leave, completely missing that underlying profits doubled.
Also we gotta understand that this gap is not spread equally across sectors either.
​Banks delivered 16% to 18% annual profit growth over the last 5 yrs with clean balance sheets, yet large bank stocks lagged. That is where most of the valuation discount sits today. Capital Goods and Auto stocks ran up alongside their profits, so there is no compression there. IT earnings slowed to single digits and prices adjusted down to match.
​A flat market during high earnings growth is not a risk signal. You pay less for every rupee of profit today than three years ago. Price follows profit gravity in the end, and every time this 6% gap opened up in the past, the next 3 to 5 yrs rewarded people who kept buying solid businesses while everyone else lost patience !

A few thoughts on how Hindus ought to argue on this topic. (This came out of my discussions with Gemini Argon 4.0)

1. Etymology: Why मूर्ति पूजा is Not "Idol Worship"

The English word "idol" derives from the Greek eidōlon—meaning a phantom, false copy, or hallucination—rooted in a worldview where matter is dead and severed from a distant Creator. By contrast, मूर्ति derives from the Sanskrit verbal root मूर्छ्, meaning "to thicken, coagulate, or assume a definite solid shape." Just as invisible water vapor condenses into solid ice without ceasing to be water, the all-pervasive, unmanifest ब्रह्मन् condenses into a localized, perceptible form out of grace. Calling मूर्ति पूजा "idol worship" is a linguistic category error that projects an alien metaphysical chasm onto a tradition of divine immanence.

2. Non-Dualist श्रुति and the Deconditioning of नाम-रूप

Iconoclasm relies on a rigid dichotomy between Creator and creation, whereas the श्रुति declares सर्वं खल्विदं ब्रह्म—everything that exists is ब्रह्मन् alone. In अद्वैत, a block of granite is nothing but ब्रह्मन् appearing under a specific नाम-रूप (name and form), just as a clay pot is nothing but clay. Because human conditioning tricks us into viewing the material world as profane and inert, प्रतीकोपासना (meditative worship via a locus) and प्राण-प्रतिष्ठा train the mind to see the Infinite shining through the finite (शालग्रामे हरिबुद्धिः). Far from shrinking God into a stone, seeing the Absolute fully present in one consecrated object shatters our dualistic conditioning, serving as a runway to eventually perceiving the entire cosmos as a living manifestation of ब्रह्मन् (सर्वात्मभाव).

3. अर्चावतार as the Zenith of सौलभ्य and वात्सल्य

Far from being a concession for the spiritually immature, आगम theology views the अर्चावतार as the pinnacle of Divine grace. Of the five modes of Divine manifestation—पर (transcendent in वैकुण्ठ or शिवलोक, beyond human reach), व्यूह (cosmological emanations), विभव (historical descents like राम and कृष्ण, accessible only to contemporaries of their era), and अन्तर्यामी (the indwelling Witness, accessible only to advanced योगिन् practitioners)—only the अर्चा breaks every barrier of time, space, and spiritual qualification. It is the ultimate expression of सौलभ्य (easy accessibility) and वात्सल्य (parental tenderness): the Omnipotent voluntarily binds Himself to stone or metal, placing Himself in the care of the devotee to be bathed, dressed, and fed, so that finite mortals can experience intimate communion with the Infinite.

4. इन्द्रिय-निग्रह Through Sensory Sublimation, Not Repression

As the भगवद्गीता notes, the path of the unmanifest (अव्यक्त) is exceedingly arduous for embodied beings whose cognitive apparatus is wired to process reality through the senses (इन्द्रिय). Rather than demanding harsh, unnatural sensory repression—which inevitably triggers psychological rebound—मूर्ति पूजा achieves true इन्द्रिय-निग्रह (mastery over the senses) by harnessing and sublimating all five sensory channels toward the Transcendent. The eyes are sanctified by beholding दर्शन and आरती, the ears by absorbing वैदिक मन्त्र chants and temple bells, the nose by inhaling camphor and तुलसी, the tongue by tasting consecrated प्रसाद, and the skin by applying भस्म, चन्दन, or तीर्थ. The senses are not starved; they are yoked to भक्ति.

5. Reconciling वेद and आगम: From मन्त्र-शरीर to विग्रह

The claim that वैदिक religion was purely aniconic while आगमिक worship is a disconnected later accretion ignores the ontological continuity between sound and form. In पूर्व मीमांसा and the वेद corpus, a देवता is understood as मन्त्र-मय—its very reality is embodied in sacred metrical vibration (मन्त्र-शरीर). The आगम texts extend this exact science of शब्द-ब्रह्मन् across dimensions: what exists acoustically as a मन्त्र manifests geometrically in two dimensions as a यन्त्र, and crystallizes in three dimensions as a विग्रह or मूर्ति. A consecrated मूर्ति is literally coagulated वैदिक sound, sculpted according to strict शिल्प शास्त्र proportions to serve as three-dimensional visual scripture.

6. The Myth of Aniconism and the Equivalence of अग्नि and अर्चा

No embodied human religion truly escapes material localization (प्रतीक). Even fiercely iconoclastic traditions orient their bodies toward specific geographic coordinates in prayer, kiss sacred stones, revere physical scriptures, or treat bread and wine as transubstantiated divinity; they practice material localization implicitly while denying it rhetorically. Internally, too, critics who champion the वैदिक यज्ञ while condemning मूर्ति पूजा commit a logical contradiction: igniting physical fire (भौतिक अग्नि), consecrating it with मन्त्र chants, and pouring घृत into it as the "mouth of the gods" uses the element of तेजस् (fire) as a physical conduit to the invisible Divine. Doing the exact same thing with consecrated पृथ्वी (earth or stone) in an अर्चा is ontologically identical—grounded in a self-aware metaphysics that distinguishes general omnipresence (व्याप्ति) from invoked special presence (विशेष-सान्निध्य).

As a long term investor one needs to understand that the cost of holding a weak (loss making) stock is more than just the loss. It is the opportunity cost of the money that could have been working in something stronger instead of holding onto something that keeps falling.
In 2022 the Nifty Smallcap 100 fell more than 30% within the year. Plenty of mid and smallcap names dropped between 30-40% from their highs. Investors who stayed in the ones that kept falling on heavy volume watched stronger stocks in the same sectors recover most of the drop within months. But the weaker stocks just kept sliding longer.
The same thing happened after the September 2024 peaks. By early 2025 the Nifty Midcap 100 was down about 14% from its high and the Smallcap 100 was down more. Many stocks  again fell over 30%. Anyone who held the ones that failed to hold recent lows on higher volume saw the better stocks start recovering first. The loss was evident. The money that could have gone into the stronger names stayed stuck.
What can we learn from these both periods:
1. Weak stocks kept making lower lows even after the index stabilised
2. Volume was higher on the down days than on any small up days
3. Stronger stocks in the same sector held above their recent lows and attracted more volume on the rise
4. People who cut the positions that refused to recover and put that money into the ones already showing higher volume on up days saw a different result. The weak stock kept costing them, the stronger one did not ! Big difference !

A low share price is not the same as a cheap price on its value. Investors should check the last 2 or 3 quarters to see if sales & profits are rising instead of falling. They should also see what the price is doing when volume picks up. Between 2018 and 2020 a lot of midcap stocks in India that looked cheap on price to earnings still fell another 40 to 60% because the numbers were getting weaker and volume was missing. The Nifty Midcap 100 itself dropped about 15% in 2018 and kept sliding into early 2020 before anything recovered. Stocks sitting at 10 to 12 times earnings kept sliding as sales and profits shrank and foreign investors stayed net sellers for months. The lower price did not help much when earnings dropped even harder and the P/E stayed the same or went up.

Before treating a fallen price as cheap, check these 3 critical things:
Is the price holding above recent lows on the days volume is higher? 
Are the up days showing more volume than the down days? 
Have sales and profits stopped falling for at least 2 quarters?

Buying just because a stock has already fallen hard has hurt more portfolios than it has helped. Stocks that recovered first usually showed higher volume on up days while the index was still weak & their profits had stopped falling !

Always remember : “A stock is cheap only when earnings are not falling.”

Once a decent pullback starts in markets the stronger stocks tend to recover sharply within 3 to 5 sessions (with rising volumes too). Weak ones keep touching lower lows & tend to take weeks or months to recover. In the 2018 Indian midcap correction, stocks that bounced inside a week with higher volume held most of their earlier gains for longer term. The ones that failed to recover in that window fell another 30–40% on average before any real bounce came. 
This brings me to the old gold investing philosophy " Sell the eggs early & hold on to the tennis balls". This critical distinction cuts the damage in many positions by a good margin.
